Each draft's own explanation

Both parties: the rider's measurement of this trip is sound, but the driver's answer to it is not an assertion the tribunal can weigh — it is a citation to a missing record, and that escalates the case instead of defeating it. The rider's case: EV-TRIP-02831, EV-GPS-02831 and EV-FARE-02831 all carry trip_id TRP-02831, so the same-trip burden under POL-RD-08(a) is met. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes: 229 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, max gap 0.0 s, so POL-RD-07(a)-(c) is not met and no independent corroboration is needed. On the governing trace figure of 29.13 km (the trip record's 29.1 is a rounded copy, which POL-RD-01 forbids using for the threshold test), the excess over the 21.9 km optimal route is 7.23 km, or 33.01% — above the 0.8 km / 20% establishment gates, so a deviation is ESTABLISHED. It reaches neither materiality gate (8.0 km, or 50%), so the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is not engaged: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 against 271 completed trips in 90 days, no pattern is established, and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral arises. POL-RD-09 gives nothing to add or correct: no ERP gantries, no airport surcharge, no fixed surcharge, the ledger reconciles to charged_total 37.07, so there is no billing-integrity correction and no POL-RD-09(4) referral. POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05, POL-RD-11 and POL-RD-12 are all out on the record (no chat messages, no amendment, METERED fare, RYDE_X). The driver's answer is an external traffic cause — 'PIE was closed' — and he names LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-02831-01 to support it. That artifact is in the bundle only as a MISSING record: payload null, admissibility status MISSING, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0, and no advisory covers the Blk 12 Telok Blangah Cres corridor in this window. POL-RD-03 therefore cannot be run — there is no advisory to test for a named road, a validity window, or a corridor exit and rejoin — and the traffic assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. So far the rider is right, but the driver has done more than assert: he has cited the missing identifier as the very artifact that covers his excuse. POL-RD-13(1) is express that it does not narrow POL-RD-10(5) where the party does cite the missing identifier, and POL-RD-10(5) makes 'a closure asserted with no traffic_advisory' a mandatory escalation trigger. An exculpatory clause (POL-RD-03) has been invoked against a cited artifact that is missing from the pool and lacks the fields that clause requires. That triggers POL-RD-10(5), and escalation is TERMINAL: it replaces the ruling, no money issues, and the disputed amount is held rather than collected or refunded. POL-RD-13(2) decides the merits only where POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged, so the rider's requested merits ruling is outweighed by the driver's own citation; the rider's alternative that NO_ACTION is impossible is accepted — nothing here restores the charge — but the disposition is the hold, not the refund. I record the merits arithmetic so the reviewer can act: on the METERED fare (surge_multiplier 1.0, read from EV-FARE-02831), recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 21.9 + 0.28 x 29.6) + 0.80 platform fee + nil ERP and nil surcharges = 29.3130, and 37.07 - 29.3130 = 7.7570, which rounds up to SGD 7.80 — a PARTIAL_REFUND had the case been decided on the merits. What would resolve the escalation: a genuine LTA traffic advisory for this trip's window that names a road or segment the optimal route traverses, with a validity window overlapping the time the trace shows the vehicle reaching that segment, and a route that leaves the optimal corridor before the affected segment and rejoins it after.
